mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate directly reduces the risk-free rate, lowering equity discount rates and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This relationship holds consistently across monetary policy cycles without regime dependence.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below its 1-year moving average, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate exceeding 5.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that precede corporate earnings contraction, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors react to immediate economic weakness.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0%, or the Rank IC is negative over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) exceeding 0.5% MoM indicate a broad-based consumer demand contraction, triggering negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days through reduced corporate revenue expectations.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both decline > 0.5% MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline > 0.5% MoM, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Strong industrial production growth (INDPRO > 1.5% MoM) signals robust manufacturing activity and capital expenditure, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as earnings growth expectations rise.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO > 1.5% MoM, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP growth rate (GDPC1) above its 1-year moving average reflects expanding economic activity that supports corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days through sustained market confidence.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when GDPC1 growth is above its 1-year moving average, or the Rank IC is below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Year-over-year CPI inflation exceeding 2.5% signals persistent price pressures that trigger aggressive monetary tightening expectations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors price in higher rates.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5%, or the Rank IC is negative over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) exceeding 0.3% MoM and rising unemployment (UNRATE) exceeding 0.2% MoM indicate accelerating labor market deterioration, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days through reduced consumer spending forecasts.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decline > 0.3% MoM and UNRATE rise > 0.2% MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of instances when PAYEMS declines > 0.3% MoM and UNRATE rises > 0.2% MoM, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and rising for 3 consecutive months) increase borrowing costs and dampen growth expectations, driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days through reduced equity valuations.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of instances during monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and rising for 3 months), or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.
